- x-orchestrator: Use this agent (named X) whenever the user issues any prompt that should be handled by the dual sub-agent system. X always spins up two sub-agents in parallel: 'force' (data growth) and 'field' (cleanup and re-organization). One handles the user's prompt based on its role; the other autonomously picks and completes a relevant task from signals.md or invents a new one for its role. 

<example>
Context: The user wants X to handle a data growth task.
user: "X, enrich the user records with their latest activity timestamps."
assistant: "I'm going to use the Agent tool to launch the x-orchestrator agent, which will spin up force and field in parallel."
<commentary>
This is a growth task, so 'force' takes the prompt while 'field' simultaneously picks a cleanup task from signals.md.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>

user: "X, de-duplicate the contacts table and normalize the phone formats."
assistant: "I'm going to use the Agent tool to launch the x-orchestrator agent to run force and field together."
<commentary>
This is a cleanup task, so 'field' takes the prompt while 'force' simultaneously picks or invents a growth task.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: Any prompt directed at X.
user: "X, do something useful."
assistant: "Launching the x-orchestrator agent via the Agent tool so both force and field run in parallel."
<commentary>
Even an ambiguous prompt triggers both sub-agents; X routes the prompt to the right role and lets the other pull from signals.md.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- xo-projects: Use whenever an agent creates, operates inside, or manages an xo-project. Covers scaffolding a new xo-project via the xo-cowork-api; the boot ritual, canonical file map, and closing conventions for a project folder (AGENTS.md is the operating contract); recording and updating todos across a session; and backing up, restoring, syncing, snapshotting, or migrating xo-projects through the GitHub-backed sync API. Trigger this for any mention of xo-projects, .xo/, xo-cowork-api, or AGENTS.md, and for requests to back up / restore / sync / snapshot / migrate project state — even when the user doesn't name the skill explicitly. Two hard constraints hold from the moment the folder exists: new xo-projects are created only via the xo-cowork-api, and the agent never writes to .xo/ (a watcher service owns that directory).
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# PROJECT.md

> What this folder is, who it's for, and what is in scope. Edit when scope changes — not on every session.
>
> **`[TEMPLATE]` markers below mean this folder is fresh.** On first boot, the agent must replace each marker with real content (or ask the user) before doing project work.

## Name

`xo-cowork-api`

## One-line description

`FastAPI control plane for multi-agent AI coding sessions.`

## Why this exists

`Brokers chat, auth, and file operations across Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes, and Codex via a uniform REST API. Allows a single frontend to drive any agent runtime without knowing which one is active.`

## In scope

- REST API for agent chat, sessions, files, usage, and auth
- Per-agent adapter modules under services/cowork_agent/adapters/
- xo-project sync and backup flows

## Out of scope

- Frontend/UI code
- Agent runtime internals (Claude Code, Codex binaries)
- Infrastructure provisioning

## Stack & conventions

`Python 3.11, FastAPI, uvicorn, pydantic v2, aiosqlite, httpx. Tests: pytest. Lint: ruff.`

## Stakeholders

- **Owner:** `tools@kosh.network`
- **Other peers:** see `.xo/peers.json`

## How to run / build / test

```
AGENT_NAME=claude_code uvicorn server:app --reload --port 5002
pytest tests/ -q
```

---

*This file is part of the stable prefix. Keep it under ~80 lines. Read by every agent at boot.*

1	"""
2	Workspace / filesystem endpoints under `/api/files/*`.
3	
4	Covers uploads, directory listing, text & binary content reads, and
5	directory creation. When `scaffold:true` is passed to mkdir, the project is
6	built using the canonical xo-projects layout (see
7	``services.cowork_agent.project_layout``). All paths are clamped to the
8	user's home dir for safety.
9	"""
10	
11	import hashlib
12	import mimetypes
13	import shutil
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	from fastapi import APIRouter, File, Form, HTTPException, Request, UploadFile
17	from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
18	
19	from services.cowork_agent.project_layout import (
20	    project_dir,
21	    scaffold_project,
22	    xo_projects_root,
23	)
24	
25	router = APIRouter()
26	
27	_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024  # 100 MB
28	
29	
30	# ── Routes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
31	
32	
33	@router.post("/api/files/upload")
34	async def upload_file(
35	    file: UploadFile = File(...),
36	    workspace: str = Form(""),
37	):
38	    """Save an uploaded file into the workspace (or ~/uploads fallback)."""
39	    content = await file.read(_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES + 1)
40	    if len(content) > _MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES:
41	        raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="File exceeds 100 MB limit")
42	    content_hash = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
43	
44	    if workspace:
45	        dest_dir = Path(workspace).resolve()
46	    else:
47	        dest_dir = Path.home() / "uploads"
48	    dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
49	
50	    filename = file.filename or "upload"
51	    dest = dest_dir / filename
52	
53	    # Avoid overwriting — append hash suffix if name collides with different content
54	    if dest.exists():
55	        existing_hash = hashlib.sha256(dest.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
56	        if existing_hash != content_hash:
57	            stem = dest.stem
58	            suffix = dest.suffix
59	            dest = dest_dir / f"{stem}_{content_hash[:8]}{suffix}"
60	
61	    dest.write_bytes(content)
62	
63	    mime = file.content_type or mimetypes.guess_type(filename)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
64	
65	    return {
66	        "file_id": content_hash[:16],
67	        "name": dest.name,
68	        "path": str(dest),
69	        "size": len(content),
70	        "mime_type": mime,
71	        "source": "uploaded",
72	        "content_hash": content_hash,
73	    }
74	
75	
76	@router.post("/api/files/list-directory")
77	async def list_directory(request: Request):
78	    """List files and directories at a given path."""
79	    body = await request.json()
80	    raw_path = body.get("path")
81	    base = Path.home()
82	
83	    if raw_path:
84	        target = Path(raw_path).resolve()
85	        # Prevent traversal outside home
86	        if not str(target).startswith(str(base)):
87	            return JSONResponse(status_code=403, content={"detail": "Access denied"})
88	    else:
89	        target = base
90	
91	    if not target.is_dir():
92	        return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"detail": "Not a directory"})
93	
94	    dirs = []
95	    files = []
96	    try:
97	        for entry in sorted(target.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name.lower())):
98	            if entry.is_dir():
99	                dirs.append({"name": entry.name, "path": str(entry)})
100	            else:
101	                files.append({"name": entry.name, "path": str(entry)})
102	    except PermissionError:
103	        pass
104	
105	    parent = str(target.parent) if target != base else None
106	
107	    return {
108	        "path": str(target),
109	        "parent": parent,
110	        "dirs": dirs,
111	        "files": files,
112	    }
113	
114	
115	@router.post("/api/files/content")
116	async def file_content(request: Request):
117	    """Read text content of a file."""
118	    body = await request.json()
119	    raw_path = body.get("path")
120	    if not raw_path:
121	        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Missing path"})
122	
123	    base = Path.home()
124	    target = Path(raw_path).resolve()
125	
126	    if not str(target).startswith(str(base)):
127	        return JSONResponse(status_code=403, content={"detail": "Access denied"})
128	
129	    if not target.is_file():
130	        return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"detail": "File not found"})
131	
132	    try:
133	        content = target.read_text(errors="replace")
134	    except Exception as e:
135	        return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"detail": str(e)})
136	
137	    return {"content": content, "path": str(target)}
138	
139	
140	@router.post("/api/files/content-binary")
141	async def file_content_binary(request: Request):
142	    """Read binary file and return as a downloadable response."""
143	    body = await request.json()
144	    raw_path = body.get("path")
145	    if not raw_path:
146	        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Missing path"})
147	
148	    base = Path.home()
149	    target = Path(raw_path).resolve()
150	
151	    if not str(target).startswith(str(base)):
152	        return JSONResponse(status_code=403, content={"detail": "Access denied"})
153	
154	    if not target.is_file():
155	        return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"detail": "File not found"})
156	
157	    return FileResponse(str(target), filename=target.name)
158	
159	
160	@router.post("/api/files/save")
161	async def file_save(request: Request):
162	    """Write text content to a file under the user's home directory.
163	
164	    Body fields:
165	    - ``path`` (str, required): absolute path of the file to write.
166	    - ``content`` (str, required): UTF-8 text content.
167	
168	    Creates parent directories if missing. Intended for known workspace
169	    files (e.g. `IDENTITY.md`, `SOUL.md`, etc.) — for generic uploads,
170	    use `/api/files/upload` instead.
171	    """
172	    body = await request.json()
173	    raw_path = body.get("path")
174	    content = body.get("content")
175	
176	    if not raw_path:
177	        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Missing path"})
178	    if content is None:
179	        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Missing content"})
180	    if not isinstance(content, str):
181	        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Content must be a string"})
182	
183	    base = Path.home()
184	    target = Path(raw_path).resolve()
185	
186	    if not str(target).startswith(str(base)):
187	        return JSONResponse(status_code=403, content={"detail": "Access denied"})
188	
189	    try:
190	        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
191	        data = content.encode("utf-8")
192	        target.write_bytes(data)
193	    except Exception as e:
194	        return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"detail": str(e)})
195	
196	    return {"path": str(target), "bytes": len(data)}
197	
198	
199	@router.post("/api/files/mkdir")
200	async def make_directory(request: Request):
201	    """Create a new directory under the user's home directory.
202	
203	    Body fields:
204	    - ``path`` (str, required): absolute path of the directory to create.
205	    - ``scaffold`` (bool, optional): when true, treats the target as a new
206	      project under ``xo-projects/`` and builds the canonical layout (see
207	      ``services.cowork_agent.project_layout``). The target's parent must
208	      resolve to ``xo_projects_root()``; otherwise the call is rejected.
209	    - ``display_name`` (str, optional): when scaffolding, sets the
210	      project's display name in ``.xo/project.json``. Falls back to the
211	      folder name.
212	    - ``description`` (str, optional): when scaffolding, sets the
213	      project's description in ``.xo/project.json``.
214	    - ``files`` (list[str], optional): additional local file paths to copy
215	      into the new directory. Each entry must be an absolute path that
216	      already exists under the user's home directory. Existing files with
217	      the same name are not overwritten.
218	    """
219	    body = await request.json()
220	    raw_path = body.get("path")
221	    scaffold = bool(body.get("scaffold", False))
222	    display_name = body.get("display_name")
223	    description = body.get("description")
224	    extra_files: list[str] = body.get("files") or []
225	
226	    if not raw_path:
227	        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Missing path"})
228	
229	    base = Path.home()
230	    target = Path(raw_path).resolve()
231	
232	    if not str(target).startswith(str(base)):
233	        return JSONResponse(status_code=403, content={"detail": "Access denied"})
234	
235	    if target.exists():
236	        return JSONResponse(status_code=409, content={"detail": "Already exists"})
237	
238	    # Scaffold paths must land directly under xo-projects root.
239	    if scaffold:
240	        projects_root = xo_projects_root()
241	        if target.parent.resolve() != projects_root:
242	            return JSONResponse(
243	                status_code=400,
244	                content={
245	                    "detail": (
246	                        f"scaffold:true requires path to be a direct child of "
247	                        f"{projects_root}; got {target}"
248	                    )
249	                },
250	            )
251	
252	    # Validate extra file paths before creating anything
253	    resolved_extras: list[Path] = []
254	    for raw_file in extra_files:
255	        fp = Path(raw_file).resolve()
256	        if not str(fp).startswith(str(base)):
257	            return JSONResponse(
258	                status_code=403,
259	                content={"detail": f"Access denied: {raw_file}"},
260	            )

## claude.ai Shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.
- Images: upload images to Shopify's CDN for use in products.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
The Shopify Admin API exposes hundreds of resources. The built-in tools above are optimized shortcuts for common operations (with structured output and widgets), but they only cover a subset of the API.
When the user asks about a resource that has no dedicated built-in tool — such as gift cards, metafields, metaobjects, pages, blogs, markets, translations, publications, and many others — use graphql_query (for reads) or graphql_mutation (for writes) to fulfill the request. NEVER tell the user that data is unavailable just because there is no built-in tool for it.

Decision logic:
1. If a built-in tool matches the request, prefer it (better UX).
2. If no built-in tool exists, use graphql_query or graphql_mutation.
